_comment: SCHEMA ONLY. The real rules live in .publish-audit.json, which is gitignored and never committed, because it spells out the exact strings it exists to keep out of this repository. Continuous integration reads the same JSON from the PUBLISH_AUDIT_RULES repository secret. See docs/DEVELOPMENT.md for how to restore or change them.
_deny: Strings that must never appear in a tracked file. This is the half that catches real leaks in a repository like this one, because a provider brand host, an account name suffix, a local network prefix and a personal drive path all look like ordinary words to a generic credential scanner. Write every pattern with a single character class, as in the example below, so the rules file does not match itself while scanning. Each rule needs a 'why'.

deny.why: illustration only. A real rule names the streaming provider whose brand appears in stream URLs, so that a copied URL cannot reach a commit
illustration only. A real rule names the maintainer's own local network prefix, which a generic scanner has no way to recognise

_allow: Expected matches, each with a written reason. An allow entry suppresses a finding everywhere, so add one only after reading the finding and deciding it is harmless. Never loosen a deny pattern to silence something.

allow.reason: illustration only. A real entry names a placeholder that replaced a genuine host, and says why that particular placeholder was chosen
